column3: Mt. Aleph is quiet now.{page_break}I hope it stays that way.{end_wait}
The curse is lifted.\nWill they start\nthe palace again?{end_wait}
No. Lord McCoy\nhas stopped the work.\nThe forest needs time.{end_wait}

He promised me
a palace.{page_break}I know what happened
in Kolima, but...
I wanted that home.{end_wait}
I remember everything.\nEven when I was a tree.{end_wait}
No one wants to cut\nthe trees near Kolima.\nI can't blame them.{end_wait}
Two travelers passed.\nOne seemed injured.{end_wait}
He was a tree once.\nI still can't forget it.{end_wait}
They barely speak now.\nHe knows why the curse\nbegan. So does she.{end_wait}
The barricade barely\nslowed anyone down.{end_wait}
The Gang of Three?\nI haven't seen them.{end_wait}
A reward is owed,\nbut it won't bring back\nwhat people endured.{end_wait}
They're telling McCoy\nwhat happened.{end_wait}
I'm so relieved.\nI could cry.{end_wait}
I'm just glad\nmy family is safe.{end_wait}
We warned them.\nThe forest was sacred.\nNo one listened.{end_wait}
The work has stopped.\nI have men to pay\nand no timber to sell.{end_wait}
McCoy says the curse\nchanged his mind.{page_break}Maybe fear taught him\nwhat reason couldn't.{end_wait}
Did the holy tree\nsurvive? Do you know?{end_now}
The work has stopped.\nSome are relieved.\nLady McCoy isn't.{end_wait}
It took centuries\nfor that tree to grow.\nWe nearly lost it.{end_wait}
I still wonder what\nthe palace might've been.{end_wait}
I miss Altin in winter.{page_break}The mines were warm\neven in the cold.{end_wait}
Father says it's warmer\nsouth of the river.{end_wait}
Are there still gems\nin Altin Mine?{end_wait}
My father has traveled\nfarther than I have.{end_wait}
The road to Kolima\nis open again.{end_wait}
Travel teaches you plenty.\nIf you survive.{end_wait}
I saw light above Imil.{page_break}Was it the lighthouse?{end_wait}
He stayed up all night.\nLook at his eyes.{end_wait}
That light came\nfrom the lighthouse.{end_wait}
It's only a lighthouse.\nWhy all the fuss?{end_wait}
I'd like to see\nthe ocean someday.{end_wait}
I'd love to sail.{page_break}I'm afraid I'd never\ncome back.{end_wait}
McCoy hired many fighters.{page_break}In the end, you were\nthe ones who helped.{end_wait}
They called themselves\nwarriors.{page_break}Then they ran.{end_wait}
That curse in Kolima.\nHorrifying, wasn't it?{end_now}
The inn is quieter now.{page_break}Still, I'm glad\nthe curse is gone.{end_wait}
There's no work here.{page_break}I'll try Xian,\nthen perhaps Tolbi.{end_wait}
The trouble is over.{page_break}Maybe I'll look\nfor work across the river.{end_wait}
I heard something\nhowling across the river.{page_break}I couldn't sleep\nafter that.{end_wait}
Bad news travels\nfaster every day.{end_wait}
Storm clouds are coming\nfrom beyond Goma.{page_break}Take shelter\nif the rain starts.{end_wait}
They pushed us aside\nand crossed the river.{page_break}We couldn't stop them.{end_wait}
We were picking fruit\nwhen the curse struck.{page_break}I never thought\nI'd see home again.{end_wait}
